questions.q: In a class of 100 students, every student has passed in one or more of the three subjects, i.e History, Economics and English. Among all the student, 24 students have passed in English only, 14 students have passed in History only 11 students have passed in both English and Economics only, and 12 students have passed in both English and History only. A total of 50 students have passed in History. If only 5 students have passed in all three subjects, then how many students have passed in Economies only?
questions.solution:
Total no. of students in the class = 100

No. of students passed in English only = 24

No. of students passed in History only = 14

No. of students passed in both English and Economics only = 11

No. of students passed in both English and History only = 12

No. of students passed in History = 50

No. of students passed in all three subjects = 5



No. of students who passed in Economics only = 100 - (50 + 24 + 11) = 100 - 85 = 15.

Hence, 15 is the correct answer.

questions.q:
Which two signs and two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

28 – 32 ÷ 2 × 8 + 34 = 132
questions.solution:
Given equation: 28 – 32 ÷ 2 × 8 + 34 = 132

1) × and -; 32 and 34

Interchanging according to the option

28 × 34 ÷ 2 – 8 + 32

= 28 × 17 – 8 + 32

= 476 – 8 + 32

= 508 – 8

= 500 ≠ 132

2) + AND -; 32 and 34

Interchanging according to the option

28 + 34 ÷ 2 × 8 – 32

= 28 + 17 × 8 – 32

= 28 + 136 – 32

= 164 – 32

= 132

3) + and -; 28 and 32

Interchanging according to the option

32 + 28 ÷ 2 × 8 – 34

= 32 + 14 × 8 – 34

= 32 + 112 – 34

= 144 – 34

= 110 ≠ 132

4) × and -; 8 and 2

Interchanging according to the option

28 × 32 ÷ 8 – 2 + 34

= 28 × 4 – 2 + 34

= 112 – 2 + 34

= 146 – 2

= 144 ≠ 132

Hence, + AND -; 32 and 34 is the correct answer

questions.q: The average height of 5 boys is 175 cm. A sixth boy joined the group and the average height of all the boys in the group now increased by one centimetre. The height of the sixth boys is:
questions.solution:

Height of sixth boys = 175 + 1 × 6 = 181

Detailed Method:

Average height of 5 boys = 175

Sum of height of 5 boys = 175 × 5 = 875

Average height of 6 boys = 176

Sum of height of 6 boys = 176 × 6 = 1056

∴ Height of 6th boy = 1056 – 875 = 181

questions.q: The distance between two stations, A and B, is 428 km. a train starts from station ‘A’ at 6:00 a.m and moves towards station ‘B’ at an average speed of 48 km/h. Another train starts from station ‘B’ at 6:20 a.m and moves towards statin ‘A’ at an average speed of 55 km/h. At what time will the trains meet?
questions.solution:
Distance between A and B = 428 km

Speed of first train = 48 km/hr

Distanced covered in 20 min by first train = 48/60 × 20 = 16 km

Remaining distance = 428 - 16 = 412 km

Speed of second train = 55 km/hr

If both train running opposite train, then relative speed = 48 + 55 = 103 km/hr

Time = distance/speed = 412/103 = 4 hr

∴ Train meet each other = 6 : 00 + 0 : 20 + 4 : 00 = 10 : 20 a. m

questions.q:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. The wild and mad elephant is claimed to have been seen in several cities.

Key Points

• The original sentence is in the active voice, the format for this will be:

• Subject + Present tense of the Verb + to have seen + Object

• This needs to be converted to the passive voice, the format for that will be:

• Object + is + Third form of the verb + to have been seen + Subject

Thus, the correct answer is option 4.

To exercise the choice to surrender before the enemy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- 'an apparently free choice where there is no real alternative.'

Key Points

• Let's understand the meaning of the given idiom:

• Hobson's choice means one has to make a choice between what is available or nothing at all. (Hobson's choice का मतलब है कि जो उपलब्ध है या बिल्कुल नहीं के बीच चुनाव करना है।)

• Example: *This is the dirtiest hotel that I have ever slept in! It is this room or out on the street, it’s Hobson’s choice.*

• From the meaning and example, we can say the correct answer is 'an apparently free choice where there is no real alternative.'

Thus *option 4 *is the most appropriate answer

Additional Information

• Let's learn about the origin of the idiom:

• This phrase has originated in the 1600s. A stable manager named Thomas Hobson (1544 -1631) would allow people to rent horses from him but gave them the choice of the next one in line or none at all.
